consensus_summary: Consensus identifies righteousness primarily as right standing before God (right relationship and conformity to His moral standard/character), most prominently as the righteousness of God/Christ credited or imputed to believers through faith rather than works; symbolic imagery includes garments/robes, breastplate, and crown. Alternatives (imputed forensic, infused transformative, covenant faithfulness, ethical-social justice, God's saving vindication) are recognized as common but secondary or contested mechanisms around the settled core.
book_summary: The book defines righteousness as right-living: God Himself is Right-Living by definition (His ways/works the measure); for those under His authority it is the doing of His commandments (the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts). Romans 4 excludes only wage-work that debts God, not obedience (complete obedience earns nothing as mere duty). Righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, yet the gift never renames wrong-living right.
consensus_core_identification: Right standing before God / conformity to His standard, primarily as imputed/credited status via faith
book_core_identification: Right-living (actual doing of God's commandments / law kept as righteous acts), given and reckoned by grace without renaming wrong-living
boundary_disagreement: Book excludes any forensic/status application that would leave wrong-living intact while still calling the person righteous; it makes actual commandment-keeping constitutive rather than merely subsequent fruit or evidence of a prior standing.
material_contradiction: Book holds that the grace-gift/reckoning of righteousness never renames wrong-living as right, which directly contradicts the dominant consensus primary (especially Protestant imputed/forensic) that declares the believer righteous (right standing) while practice may still include sin (simul iustus et peccator).
rationale: Minimum cores are not equivalent: consensus centers on right standing (often a declared/imputed status received by faith, with living as related or subsequent), while the book centers on right-living itself (obedience/commandments as the thing given and worn). Accepting the book replaces the consensus identification rather than merely narrowing its cases; the explicit denial that the gift can cover/rename wrong-living produces a material contradiction with the primary forensic reading, even though both share grace-reckoning language, garment imagery, and rejection of meritorious wage-work. Overlap on secondary alternatives (ethical/transformative) does not salvage core equivalence.
strongest_objection: Key Pauline texts printed (Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9) are classically read as forensic imputation of status apart from works, so the book's prioritization of commandment-keeping (Deut 6:25; 1 John 3:7) and duty (Luke 17) may conflate or subordinate justification to sanctification against the consensus primary.
